acceptance.claim: Due TS rows are marked revived with reason SPO and remark 'Auto-revived on due date'; if another suspension is still active, the remaining suspension with the latest date_of_suspension is copied to VON and eVON, and VON.due_date_of_revival takes the furthest due date of the remaining suspensions (eVON gets no due date).

acceptance.claim: After revival, TS-PDP is re-applied for an unpaid notice that has a Pending furnish application (status P). TS-HST and TS-CLV are also re-applied ... (OCMS-DF-2026-117); this part is not part of the claim.

'Unpaid' here is isPaidNotice() = active permanent PS-FP or PS-PRA (:1245-1250), which differs from the 'paid' definition in acceptance 1 (crs_reason / epr PRA, :387/:390); for a PS-FP/PS-PRA notice the code patches VON instead (:984-988). Pending furnish = f.status = 'P' at :924, processTS call at :1011-1014. The HST/CLV sentence is a disclaimer, not a testable claim.
acceptance.fix_en: After revival, TS-PDP is re-applied on a notice whose revived TS row has reason PDP, when the notice has no active PS-FP or PS-PRA and has a Pending furnish application (status P).

overlap.reason: 19.9 is the officer-facing revival summary/confirm screen; 52.1 is a headless cron. Different trigger, but URA may argue the revival write logic (TS revive, VON/eVON sync) is the 'proceed to revive' part of 19.9.
19.1 is an officer choosing the revival type (TS/PS/reduction). Auto revival is TS only with no officer input; low text overlap, but shared revival helpers may be read as the same capability.
19.15 is PLUS sending revival requests. 52.1 has no PLUS input at all.

The user story of 52.1 itself (TS-HST/TS-CLV re-apply after expiry) overlaps 14.28 'continue the TS when the existing suspension expires'; the claim must stay on base revival + TS-PDP and 14.28 should not be cited.
